title: From Shallow Humor to Metaphor: Towards Label-Free Harmful Meme Detection via LMM Agent Self-Improvement
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to perform zero-shot, label-free detection of harmful memes (which include discrimination and hate speech targeting individuals or communities based on religion, race, gender, etc.). Specific to religion, it analyzed the model's ability to extrapolate 'experiences' from explicit anti-Muslim memes to accurately detect more subtle or implicit forms of harmful anti-Muslim content.
findings: The paper found that their proposed framework, ALARM, can successfully help Large Multimodal Models learn from memes containing explicit religious discrimination (e.g., explicit anti-Muslim messaging) to autonomously generate high-level detection references. These references significantly improve the LMM's ability to detect much more subtle and implicit harmful memes targeting the same religious group, effectively doing so without the need for labeled training data.
